title: DashboardOperational
wrapsNative: MonarchDashboardGrid (androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.grid.LazyVerticalGrid) of a MonarchStatCard row (androidx.compose.foundation.layout.FlowRow), MonarchWidget sections with MonarchBadge, MonarchLineChart, MonarchLeaderboard and MonarchActivityTimeline
summary: The home screen of an operational product (incidents, tickets, alerts): key figures, what needs attention, the trend, team load and recent activity, as sections of a MonarchDashboardGrid.
whenToUse: As the home screen of a product whose work arrives continuously, and for a team lead's overview of live work and load.
whenNotToUse: For a sales, hiring or campaign home use the DashboardPipeline recipe; for a set of assets use DashboardPortfolio; for a person's own work use DashboardPersonalWork.
api: MonarchDashboardGrid(items = sections, key = { it }, itemLabel = { it }, modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize(), span = { if (it == "Key figures") MonarchDashboardGridSpan.Full else MonarchDashboardGridSpan.One }) { section -> when (section) { "Key figures" -> FlowRow(maxItemsInEachRow = 2) { MonarchStatCard(…) }; "Needs attention" -> MonarchWidget(title = …, onViewAll = …) { rows with MonarchBadge(tone = Danger or Warning) }; "Trend" -> MonarchLineChart(title = …, categories = …, series = …); "Team load" -> MonarchWidget(title = …) { MonarchLeaderboard(entries = …) }; else -> MonarchWidget(title = "Recent activity") { MonarchActivityTimeline(…) } } }

options.name: sections
options.description: The sections in order; leave out what the product has no data for. The web's slots are status, attention, queue, trend, workload, upcoming and activity.

options.name: key figures
options.description: The KPI row, as the first full-span item (the KpiRow recipe).

options.name: needs attention / my queue / coming up
options.description: Short lists of items with their status as a badge in words, linking to the full list with View all.

options.name: trend
options.description: How the workload moves over time, with its table view.

options.name: insights
options.description: Rule or AI findings as a full-span item under the key figures.

states.name: loading or failed section
states.description: MonarchWidget with state = Loading or Failed and onRetry, MonarchStatCard with loading, or the chart's status, per section.

states.name: editing
states.description: MonarchDashboardGrid with editing = true shows arrange bars to move sections, with TalkBack actions.

appearance: Widgets and stat cards on the surface color with the subtle border; statuses as badges in the danger and warning tones; the line chart and leaderboard bars in the data colors. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web DashboardOperational is one template with a header (title, scope, period, actions), a KPI row, an insight strip and named slots in a responsive grid. On Android it is a recipe the app owns: MonarchDashboardGrid is the screen's scrolling list (one column on a phone, more from 1024dp, rearrangeable with editing), and each section is a MonarchWidget or another Monarch part. The title, period and actions belong to the screen's TopAppBar. Lazy parts such as MonarchActivityTimeline get a bounded height inside a grid item. Section structure (C-050, aligned with the iOS recipe): the same sections in the same order as the web template and iOS: a summary line with an alert banner, the key figures (four stat cards), the insight strip, then Status, Needs attention, My queue, Trend, Team load, Coming up and Recent activity, with Needs attention and Trend two columns wide on a tablet. Remaining differences from iOS: the summary, key figures and insights are the first full-width items of MonarchDashboardGrid, because on Android the grid is the screen's one scrolling list (iOS stacks them above the grid in a ScrollView); the title, period and actions go to the TopAppBar instead of the navigation bar and toolbar; status icons are app slots because Monarch bundles no icons.
accessibility: Each widget's title is a heading and the key figures are one traversal group named after the section.
Statuses are badges in words, never color alone.
The line chart has a summary and a table view; the leaderboard reads each name with its value and rank.
Rearranging sections has TalkBack custom actions in MonarchDashboardGrid, so dragging is never required.
edgeCases: Keep each section short and link to the full list with View all.
A lazy timeline inside a grid item needs a bounded height.
Never put the grid inside a vertically scrolling parent; it is the screen's list.
